L144: Let $\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$ be the ground state vector of $H_{\Lambda}$ normalized so that $\langle\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda},\Omega_{\Lambda,0}\rangle=1$ (i.e., $\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}:=\Omega_{\Lambda}/\langle\Omega_{\Lambda},\Omega_{\Lambda,0}\rangle$).
L145: Initially the non-degeneracy of the ground state and its non-orthogonality to $\Omega_{\Lambda,0}$ is clear from the usual finite-volume perturbation theory for sufficiently weak perturbations in each particular volume, and it can be shown that the estimate for the perturbation which ensures this property can actually be chosen uniform in the volume. Let $\{v^{(\Lambda,gs)}_{I}\in{\mathcal{H}}_{I}^{\prime}\}_{\emptyset\neq I\subset\Lambda}$ be the corresponding collection such that
L146:  | $$\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}=\exp\bigl(\sum_{\emptyset\neq I\subset\Lambda}\widehat{v}^{(\Lambda,gs)}_{I}\bigr)\Omega_{\Lambda,0}.$$  |
L147: ###### Lemma 1.
L148: 
L149: For any $\epsilon>0$, if $\sup_{x}\|\phi_{x}\|$ is sufficiently small then
L150: 
L151:  | $$\max_{x\in\Lambda}\sum_{I\subset\Lambda:x\in I}\|H_{I,0}v_{I}^{(\Lambda,gs)}\|\epsilon^{-(d_{I}+1)}\leq 1,$$  |  | (8)

L154: The idea of the proof is to rewrite the Schrödinger equation $H_{\Lambda}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}=E_{\Lambda}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$ as a fixed point equation for a suitable (non-linear) mapping on the space of collections, which is then shown to be a contraction in the set specified by Eq.(【40†8】).

L159: For any $v$, there exists a unique collection such that (【41†9】) holds: indeed, if we introduce the operators $P_{\Lambda,I}:{\mathcal{H}}_{\Lambda}\to{\mathcal{H}}_{I}^{\prime}$ by
L160: 
L161:  | $$u=\sum_{I\subset\Lambda}(P_{\Lambda,I}u)\otimes\Omega_{\Lambda\setminus I,0},\quad\forall u\in{\mathcal{H}}_{\Lambda},$$  |

L164:  | $\displaystyle v_{K}$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle P_{\Lambda,K}\sum_{J\subset\Lambda}\widehat{v}_{J}\Omega_{\Lambda,0}$  |  | (10)

L173:  | $$\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda,0}\widehat{v}_{I}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}=\widehat{H_{I,0}v_{I}}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}.$$  |  | (12)

L175: For the renormalized perturbation $\widetilde{\Phi}_{\Lambda}$ we then have
L176:  | $\displaystyle\widetilde{\Phi}_{\Lambda}\widehat{v}_{I}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle(\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda}-\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda,0})\widehat{v}_{I}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$  |
L177:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda}\widehat{v}_{I}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}-\widehat{H_{I,0}v_{I}}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$  |
L178:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle[\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda},\widehat{v}_{I}]\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}-\widehat{H_{I,0}v_{I}}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$  |
L179:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle[H_{\Lambda,0},\widehat{v}_{I}]\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}+[\Phi_{\Lambda},\widehat{v}_{I}]\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}-\widehat{H_{I,0}v_{I}}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$  |
L180:  |  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle[\Phi_{\Lambda},\widehat{v}_{I}]\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}.$  |
L181: It is convenient to write the operator $\widetilde{\Phi}_{\Lambda}$ in the form
L182: 
L183:  | $$\widetilde{\Phi}_{\Lambda}\widehat{v}_{I}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}=\sum_{J\subset\Lambda}\widehat{(F_{\Lambda}v_{I})_{J}}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$$  |  | (13)

L185: with some $(F_{\Lambda}v_{I})_{J}\in{\mathcal{H}}^{\prime}_{J}$, thereby expanding the image vector as in (【41†9】). Using (【42†10】), we find that
L186:  | $\displaystyle(F_{\Lambda}v_{I})_{J}$  | $\displaystyle=$  | $\displaystyle P_{\Lambda,J}\exp\bigl(-\sum_{\emptyset\neq K\subset\Lambda}\widehat{v}^{(\Lambda,gs)}_{K}\bigr)[\Phi_{\Lambda},\widehat{v}_{I}]\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}$  |

L188: Expanding this expression into a commutator series and using Lemma 1, one finds that

L190:  | $$\sum_{J\subset\Lambda}\|(F_{\Lambda}v_{I})_{J}\|\epsilon^{-(d_{J;I}+1)}\leq c\sup_{x}\|\phi_{x}\||I|\|v_{I}\|,$$  |  | (14)
L191: where by $d_{J;I}$ we denote the minimal length of a graph connecting all sites in $J$ to some sites in $I$. In particular, this estimate shows that $\widetilde{\Phi}_{\Lambda}$ is a relatively bounded, in some special sense, perturbation of $\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda,0}$. Indeed, we introduce a new norm ${|\!|\!|}\cdot{|\!|\!|}$ in ${\mathcal{H}}_{\Lambda}$ by

L193:  | $${|\!|\!|}\sum_{I\subset\Lambda}\widehat{u}_{I}\widetilde{\Omega}_{\Lambda}{|\!|\!|}:=\sum_{I\subset\Lambda}\|u_{I}\|.$$  |

L197: We assume that $\sup_{x}\|\phi_{x}\|$ is small so that $c\sup_{x}\|\phi_{x}\|<1$. If $z\in\mathbb{C}$ lies outside of the union of circles standing on the r.h.s. of (【33†4】), then ${|\!|\!|}\widetilde{\Phi}_{\Lambda}(\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda,0}-z)^{-1}{|\!|\!|}<1$ and hence the resolvent $(\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda}-z)^{-1}$ exists and is given by the exponentially convergent series
L198:  | $$(\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda,0}-z)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(-1)^{k}(\widetilde{\Phi}_{\Lambda}(\widetilde{H}_{\Lambda,0}-z)^{-1})^{k}.$$  |  | (15)

L200: That proves the spectral estimate (【33†4】).

L202: We consider now the thermodynamic limit $\Lambda\nearrow{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}$. It easily follows from the proof of Lemma 1 that the quantities $v_{I}^{(\Lambda,gs)}$, defining the ground state in finite volumes, have limits
L203:  | $$v_{I}^{(\infty,gs)}:=\lim_{\Lambda\nearrow{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}}v_{I}^{(\Lambda,gs)}.$$  |
L204: 
L205: Using this, Theorem 2 follows immediately by cluster expansions. As a by-product of cluster expansions, one obtains an exponential decay of correlations in the ground state:
L206:  | $$|\omega_{\infty}(A_{1}A_{2})-\omega_{\infty}(A_{1})\omega_{\infty}(A_{2})|\leq c^{|\Lambda_{1}|+|\Lambda_{2}|}\epsilon^{\,\mathrm{dist}\,(\Lambda_{1},\Lambda_{2})}\|A_{1}\|\|A_{2}\|,\;\;\;A_{i}\in\mathcal{B}({\mathcal{H}}_{\Lambda_{i}})$$  |  | (16)
L207: 
L208: Iterating this inequality, one finds that
L209:  |  |  | $\displaystyle|\omega_{\infty}(A_{1}\cdots A_{n})-\omega_{\infty}(A_{1})\cdots\omega_{\infty}(A_{n})|$  |  | (17)
L210:  |  | $\displaystyle\leq$  | $\displaystyle(n-1)c^{|\Lambda_{1}|+\ldots+|\Lambda_{n}|}\epsilon^{\min_{i\neq j}\,\mathrm{dist}\,(\Lambda_{i},\Lambda_{j})},\qquad A_{i}\in\mathcal{B}({\mathcal{H}}_{\Lambda_{i}}).$  |
L211: Now we discuss the thermodynamic limit of the Hamiltonian. Recall that $({\mathcal{H}}_{\infty},\pi_{\infty},\Omega_{\infty})$ is the GNS triple associated with the ground state $\omega_{\infty}$. The limiting Hamiltonian $H_{\infty}$ is conventionally defined on the vectors of the form $\pi_{\infty}(A)\Omega_{\infty}$, with $A\in\mathcal{A}_{\infty}$ such that $[H,A]\in\mathcal{A}_{\infty}$, by
L212: 
L213:  | $$H_{\infty}\pi_{\infty}(A)\Omega_{\infty}:=\pi_{\infty}([H,A])\Omega_{\infty}.$$  |
L214: It is convenient to take $A=\widehat{u}_{I}$ here. Consider the space $\mathcal{U}$ of finite linear combinations of operators $\widehat{u}_{I}$. It is easy to see that the set $\pi_{\infty}(\mathcal{U})\Omega_{\infty}$ is dense in ${\mathcal{H}}_{\infty}$. Extending the formulas (【44†11】),(【45†12】),(【46†13】), we have
L215:  | $$H_{\infty}\pi_{\infty}(\widehat{u}_{I})\Omega_{\infty}=\pi_{\infty}(\widehat{H_{I,0}u_{I}})\Omega_{\infty}+\pi_{\infty}\Bigl(\sum_{J\subset{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}},|J|<\infty}\widehat{(F_{\infty}u_{I})_{J}}\Bigr)\Omega_{\infty},$$  |  | (18)
L216: 
L217: where
L218: 
L219:  | $$(F_{\infty}u_{I})_{J}:=\lim_{\Lambda\nearrow{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}}(F_{\Lambda}u_{I})_{J}.$$  |
L220: By this formula the operator $H_{\infty}$ is densely defined on the subspace spanned by vectors $\pi_{\infty}(\widehat{u}_{I})\Omega_{\infty}$ with $u_{I}\in{\mathcal{H}}_{I}^{\prime}\cap\,\mathrm{Dom}\,(H_{I,0})$. The estimate (【43†14】) remains valid for the limiting quantities $(F_{\infty}u_{I})_{J}$, so the resolvent expansion of the form (【47†15】) for $(H_{\infty}-z)^{-1}$, with the same values of $z$ as before, is exponentially convergent on vectors from $\pi_{\infty}(\mathcal{U})\Omega_{\infty}$.
L221: The essential self-adjointness of $H_{\infty}$ and the resolvent convergence (【48†6】) follow by standard arguments.
L222: ## 3 Proof of Theorem 4
L223: 
L224: The orthogonal projector onto the spectral subspace ${\mathcal{H}}_{1}$, corresponding to the neighborhood of the point $\mu$ as defined in the Introduction, is given by
L225: 
L226:  | $$P_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}=-(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_{\gamma}(H_{\infty}-z)^{-1}dz,$$  |
L227: where $\gamma$ is a contour in the complex plane surrounding this neighborhood. Since $\gamma$ lies outside of the union of circles standing on the r.h.s. of (【33†4】), we can use the resolvent expansion (【47†15】) to estimate projections of vectors $\widehat{u}_{I}\Omega_{\infty}$. For the normalized eigenvector $w_{x}$ of $h$ at the site $x$, using estimate (【43†14】) we obtain
L228:  | $$P_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}\widehat{w}_{x}\Omega_{\infty}=\widehat{w}_{x}\Omega_{\infty}+\sum_{I}\widehat{v}_{I}^{(w_{x})}\Omega_{\infty},$$  |  | (19)
L229: 
L230: with some vectors $v_{I}^{(w_{x})}$ such that
L231: 
L232:  | $$\sum_{I}\|H_{I,0}v_{I}^{(w_{x})}\|\epsilon^{-(d_{I\cup\{x\}}+1)}\leq 1.$$  |  | (20)
L233: The first term in (【49†19】) comes from the leading term in the resolvent expansion; the second term, coming from the rest of the expansion, is small due to (【43†14】). It is easy to see that the vectors $P_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}\widehat{w}_{x}\Omega_{\infty}$ are total in ${\mathcal{H}}_{1}$.
L234: Indeed, since $\mathcal{U}\Omega_{\infty}$ is dense in ${\mathcal{H}}_{\infty}$, it suffices to show that for any $u_{I}$ we can expand $P_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}\widehat{u}_{I}\Omega_{\infty}$ as a sum of $P_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}\widehat{w}_{x}\Omega_{\infty},x\in{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}$, with some coefficients.
L235: For any $u_{I}$, if $|I|>1$, or if $I=\{x\}$ and $\langle u_{x},w_{x}\rangle=0$ (let us call for the moment such vectors $\widehat{u}_{I}\Omega_{\infty}$ ‘irrelevant’, as opposed to the ‘relevant’ $\widehat{w}_{x}\Omega_{\infty}$), we have an expansion similar to (【49†19】), but with the vanishing leading term:
L236:  | $$P_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}\widehat{u}_{I}\Omega_{\infty}=\sum_{J}\widehat{v}_{J}^{(u_{I})}\Omega_{\infty},$$  |  | (21)
L237: 
L238: where
L239: 
L240:  | $$\sum_{J}\|H_{J,0}v_{J}^{(u_{I})}\|\epsilon^{-(d_{J;I}+1)}\leq\|u_{I}\|.$$  |
L241: In particular, $\sum_{J}\|v_{J}^{(u_{I})}\|\leq\|u_{I}\|/2$ for such $u_{I}$. Now, on the r.h.s. of (【50†21】), we single out the contribution spanned by $\widehat{w}_{x}\Omega_{\infty},x\in{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}},$ and apply $P_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}$ to both sides of the equality.
L242: Since $P_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}^{2}=P_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}$, we see that the projection of an irrelevant vector is represented as a sum of relevant projections plus projections of irrelevant vectors with a smaller total norm; the iteration of this procedure yields the desired expansion of $P_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}\widehat{u}_{I}\Omega_{\infty}$ in terms of $P_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}\widehat{w}_{x}\Omega_{\infty}$.
L243: Now we orthogonalize the vectors $P_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}\widehat{w}_{x}\Omega_{\infty},x\in{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}$. Let $G$ be the Gram matrix of this family:
L244: 
L245:  | $$G_{xy}=\langle P_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}\widehat{w}_{x}\Omega_{\infty},P_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}\widehat{w}_{y}\Omega_{\infty}\rangle.$$  |
L246: 
L247: Using the decay of correlation estimate (【51†16】) and the expansion (【49†19】) with the estimate (【52†20】), one finds that
L248: 
L249:  | $$|G_{xy}-\delta_{xy}|\leq\epsilon^{|x-y|+1}.$$  |  | (22)
L250: We obtain an orthogonal family $\xi_{x}$ by applying $G^{-1/2}$ to the vectors $P_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}\widehat{w}_{x}\Omega_{\infty}$:
L251: 
L252:  | $$\xi_{x}=\sum_{y}G^{-1/2}_{xy}P_{{\mathcal{H}}_{1}}\widehat{w}_{y}\Omega_{\infty}.$$  |

L254: It is easy to see that the exponential estimate (【53†22】) for $G$ implies similar estimate for $G^{-1/2}$; as a result, we have for $\xi_{x}$ an expansion analogous to (【49†19】) with an exponential estimate analogous to (【52†20】):
L255:  | $$\xi_{x}=\widehat{w}_{x}\Omega_{\infty}+\sum_{I}\widehat{v}_{I}^{(\xi_{x})}\Omega_{\infty},$$  |  | (23)
L256:

L260: We have thus shown that ${\mathcal{H}}_{1}$ is a one-particle subspace, and it only remains to check that the energy-momentum relation is analytic. It follows from the exponential decay of $\langle H_{\infty}\xi_{x},\xi_{y}\rangle$ at $|x-y|\to\infty$, which in turn follows from the above expansion (【54†23】),(【55†24】) using decay of correlations (【51†16】).
L261: ## 4 Proof of Theorem 5
L262: 
L263: An important point in the proof of Theorem 5 is the observation that distant excitations of the ground state evolve independently. Recall that the Hamiltonian $H_{\infty}$ is defined by $H_{\infty}A\Omega_{\infty}=[H,A]\Omega_{\infty},$ where $A$ is any local operator such that $[H,A]$ is bounded. If operators $A_{i}$ act on ${\mathcal{H}}_{I_{i}},i=1,\ldots,n,$ and the distance between different $I_{i}$’s is greater than the range of interaction, then
L264:  | $$[H,A_{1}A_{2}\cdots A_{n}]=A_{2}\cdots A_{n}[H,A_{1}]+\ldots+A_{1}\cdots A_{n-1}[H,A_{n}].$$  |
L265: 
L266: In particular, if $A_{i}=\widehat{v}_{I_{i}}$ with some $v_{I_{i}}\in{\mathcal{H}}_{I_{i}}^{\prime}\cap\,\mathrm{Dom}\,(H_{I_{i},0})$, where $I_{i}$’s are separated by distances not less than the interaction range, then
L267:  | $$H_{\infty}\widehat{v}_{I_{1}}\widehat{v}_{I_{2}}\cdots\widehat{v}_{I_{n}}\Omega_{\infty}=\widehat{v}_{I_{2}}\cdots\widehat{v}_{I_{n}}H_{\infty}\widehat{v}_{I_{1}}\Omega_{\infty}+\ldots+\widehat{v}_{I_{1}}\cdots\widehat{v}_{I_{n-1}}H_{\infty}\widehat{v}_{I_{n}}\Omega_{\infty}.$$  |  | (25)
L268: In the previous section we found a basis $\xi_{x}$ in the one-particle subspace ${\mathcal{H}}_{1}$, whose vectors have the well-localized expansion (【54†23】),(【55†24】). The time evolution of a quasi-particle state is straightforwardly described in the momentum picture, where such a state is identified with a function on the torus $\mathbb{T}^{\nu}$ of quasi-momenta.
L269: In this picture we can form one-particle states, propagating as wave packets in certain directions, and, using (【55†24】), these states can be shown to be spatially well-localized. If we consider a few such wave packets, moving in different direction away from each other, then in the distant past or future they will form far separated excitations of the ground state.
L270: By (【56†25】), the evolution of the corresponding “product” state in ${\mathcal{H}}_{\infty}$ is then asymptotically close to the product of respective one-particle evolutions. Precisely this relation can be stated as the existence of isometric wave operators intertwining the second quantization of the one particle evolution with the evolution generated by $H_{\infty}$ in a subspace of ${\mathcal{H}}_{\infty}$.
L271: Following the standard setting of scattering theory for a pair of Hilbert spaces (see [【38†21】]), we begin by introducing the operator $T:\mathcal{F}\to\mathcal{H}_{\infty}$, defining an approximate “product” of one-particle states. Let $\mathcal{F}_{n}$ be the $n$-particle subspace of the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal{F}$. The normalized symmetrized products $(\xi_{x_{1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes\xi_{x_{n}})^{sym}$ form an orthonormal basis in $\mathcal{F}_{n}$. Using expansion (【54†23】), we set
L272:  | $$T:(\xi_{x_{1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes\xi_{x_{n}})^{sym}\mapsto\prod_{k=1}^{n}(\widehat{w}_{x_{k}}+\sum_{I}\widehat{v}_{I}^{(\xi_{x_{k}})})\Omega_{\infty}.$$  |
L273: This operator does not generally extend to a bounded operator on $\mathcal{F}$, but it is well-defined on vectors of the form $\sum_{n=1}^{N}k_{x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}}(\xi_{x_{1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes\xi_{x_{n}})^{sym}$, where $N$ is finite and $\sum_{n=1}^{N}|k_{x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}}|<\infty$; this will be sufficient for us. In the Fock space $\mathcal{F}$ we find a dense subset $S$ such that the quantities
L274: 
L275:  | $$W_{t}{\bf f}:=\exp\{itH_{\infty}\}T\exp\{-itH_{f}\}{\bf f}$$  |
L276: are well-defined for ${\bf f}\in S$ and $t\in\mathbb{R}$, and there exist isometric limits
L277: 
L278:  | $$W_{\pm}{\bf f}:=\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}W_{t}{\bf f}.$$  |  | (26)
L279: 
L280: Then $W_{\pm}:\mathcal{F}\to H_{\infty}$ are the desired isometric wave operators, implementing the intertwining relation $W_{\pm}H_{f}=H_{\infty}W_{\pm}$. The intertwining relation for lattice translations, $W_{\pm}U_{f,x}=U_{x}W_{\pm}$, is obvious because $TU_{f,x}=U_{x}T$.
L281: The dense set $S$ is spanned by collections of quasi-particles forming smooth wave packets drifting away from each other. Precisely, recall that by definition of the one-particle subspace we have a unitary $V:{\mathcal{H}}_{1}\to L_{2}(\mathbb{T}^{\nu})$ defining the momentum picture.
L282: If $f\in{\mathcal{H}}_{1}$ is such that $Vf\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{T}^{\nu})$, then a standard stationary phase estimate shows that, roughly speaking, this wave packet propagates with velocities from the set $\{2\pi\nabla m(p)|p\in\,\mathrm{supp}\,(Vf)\}$:
L283: ###### Lemma 2 ([【38†21】]).
L284: 
L285: Let $Vf\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{T}^{\nu})$ and $\mathcal{O}\subset\mathbb{R}^{\nu}$ be an open set containing $\{2\pi\nabla m(p)|p\in\,\mathrm{supp}\,(Vf)\}$. Then for arbitrarily large $a$ there exists a constant $c=c(f,\mathcal{O},a)$ such that
L286: 
L287:  | $$|\langle\exp\{itH_{\infty}\}f,\xi_{x}\rangle|=\Bigl|\int_{\mathbb{T}^{\nu}}e^{itm(p)-2\pi i\langle x,p\rangle}Vf(p)dp\Bigr|\leq c(1+|x|+|t|)^{-a}$$  |
L288: 
L289: for $x/t\notin\mathcal{O}$.
L290: This Lemma shows that if $\exp\{itH_{\infty}\}f$ is expanded as $\sum_{x\in{\mathbb{Z}^{\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\nu}}{{}}}}}k_{x}\xi_{x}$, then the coefficients $k_{x}$ are small for $x\notin\{2\pi t\nabla m(p)|p\in\,\mathrm{supp}\,(Vf)\}$.
L291: 
L292: Consider now the subset $S_{n}\subset\mathcal{F}_{n}$ formed by vectors $(f_{1}\otimes\cdots\otimes f_{n})^{sym}$ such that $Vf_{k}$ are $C^{\infty}$ and
L293:  | $$\nabla m(p_{k})\neq\nabla m(p_{l})\text{ for
L294: }p_{k}\in\,\mathrm{supp}\,(Vf_{k}),p_{l}\in\,\mathrm{supp}\,(Vf_{l}),k\neq l.$$  |
L295: 
L296: We define $S$ as the linear span of $\cup_{n}S_{n}$. Since the energy-momentum relation $m(p)$ is a non-constant analytic function, it is easy to see that $S_{n}$ is a total subset of $\mathcal{F}_{n}$ and hence $S$ is dense in $\mathcal{F}$.
L297: We will show now that the wave operators (【57†26】) exist for ${\bf f}\in S_{n}$ (and hence for ${\bf f}\in S$). By the Cook method, it suffices to prove that
L298: 
L299:  | $$\int_{\mathbb{R}}\|(H_{\infty}T-TH_{f})\exp\{-itH_{f}\}{\bf f}\|dt<\infty.$$  |  | (27)
L300: 
L301: The question is whether the integrand falls off fast enough as $t\to\infty$. We will see that it is actually $o(|t|^{a})$ for any $a$.
L302: 
L303: Note first that for any $f\in{\mathcal{H}}_{1}$ we can expand $f_{t}:=\exp\{-itH_{\infty}\}f$ as
L304:  | $$f_{t}=\sum_{I}\widehat{v}_{I}^{(f_{t})}\Omega_{\infty}$$  |  | (28)
L305: 
L306: by first expanding $f_{t}$ in $\xi_{x}$ and then expanding the latter as in (【54†23】). If $Vf\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{T}^{\nu})$ and $\mathcal{O}$ is an open vicinity of $\{2\pi\nabla m(p)|p\in\,\mathrm{supp}\,(Vf)\}$, then it follows from Lemma 3 and estimate (【55†24】) that in (【58†28】) the contribution from the terms with $I\not\subset t\mathcal{O}$ is small: precisely, for any $a$
